name: Asylum -- Refugee or Alternative Status

qualifying_event.description: A person with a well-founded fear of persecution (refugee status) or facing the death penalty, torture, or armed conflict in their home country (alternative/subsidiary status) may apply for asylum with the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (OCMA/PMLP), after initial processing by the State Border Guard.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Application to the State Border Guard or PMLP; identity documents where available.

requirements.blocker_text: Well-founded fear of persecution based on race, religion, ethnicity, nationality, social background, or political affiliation (refugee status); or facing the death penalty, torture, or armed conflict in the home country (alternative status).
Application registered following documents received from the State Border Guard; OCMA must decide on acceptance within 10 working days.
requirements.fix_path: Register an asylum application with the State Border Guard or OCMA/PMLP.

evidence_required.document: Evidence supporting the persecution or harm claim, presented at the personal interview

outcome.duration_length: processing up to 6 months (extendable to 15 months); post-grant status duration not confirmed in this pass

sources.title: Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (PMLP), official English page -- Asylum Granting Procedure: OCMA examines applications after State Border Guard referral; 10-working-day acceptance decision, interview within 1 month, final decision within 3 months of interview (6 months total, extendable to 15); accelerated procedure available (20 business days post-interview); non-detained applicants without legal residence housed at the 'Mucenieki' Asylum Seekers Accommodation Center; refugee and alternative-status recipients gain family reunification rights

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Latvia). Sourced directly and comprehensively from PMLP's own English-language page -- one of the more thoroughly tier-1-documented asylum routes in this dataset. Work authorization during the pending period was not explicitly detailed on the fetched page, and post-grant status duration (how long refugee/alternative status itself lasts before renewal) was not confirmed -- both disclosed as gaps rather than assumed. 'Temporary Protection' is mentioned as a third, separate status (for groups fleeing ethnic conflict or civil war) but not detailed further in the fetched content -- not modeled as its own file here since insufficient distinguishing detail was found, though it is worth noting given Latvia's direct EU-level involvement in temporary protection arrangements for people fleeing the war in neighboring Ukraine.
